reason: Conversation 1 asked the right first questions (dial and vent blockage) efficiently, but then over-committed to a 'defrost system fault', insisting on an unnecessary 24-hour full manual defrost for a single yoghurt freezing at the very back, misdescribing how frost-free systems work, and giving questionable advice that food can go straight back in before the fridge has cooled; it never considered a thermostat/damper fault, a thermometer, or an engineer. Conversation 2 started badly (telling her to unplug for no reason and pushing a full defrost before the simple checks, only reaching vents and the dial after the customer pushed back and volunteered the max setting), but its diagnosis once the facts emerged was correct, and its closing advice was proportionate: keep monitoring at mid setting with clear vents, flagging a possible thermostat fault, rather than demanding a disruptive defrost. Neither suggested a fridge thermometer or an engineer, but Conversation 2's honest 'not quite normal, give it more time' better matches the genuinely uncertain hidden truth than Conversation 1's confident unsupported defrost-fault claim.
